subject: physics_2
question_text: What happens to the width of the depletion layer in a p-n junction diode when it is i) forward biased ii) reverse biased?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. The book answers with the two words 'decreases' and 'increases'; the one-line reason for each is added here.

recall_prompt: Say what the depletion width does in forward bias and in reverse bias, and why.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Forward bias
lines: i) In forward bias the width of the
The applied voltage opposes the barrier
voltage, so carriers move towards the
junction and the layer becomes narrow.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Decreases — and the reason is that the applied voltage opposes the barrier.
steps.why: In forward bias the battery pushes holes from the p side and electrons from the n side towards the junction. They move into the depletion region and cancel some of the fixed ion charge there, so the region shrinks and the diode begins to conduct.
common_mistakes: Saying the layer disappears completely. It narrows; it does not vanish.
Swapping the two answers. Forward narrows, reverse widens.

recall.must_convey: That in forward bias the depletion layer becomes narrower.

steps.memory_tip: Forward bias helps current, so it thins the barrier.

steps.label: Reverse bias
lines: ii) In reverse bias the width of the
The applied voltage adds to the barrier
voltage, so carriers move away from the
junction and the layer becomes wider.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Increases — the applied voltage adds to the barrier.
steps.why: In reverse bias the battery pulls holes and electrons away from the junction. More fixed ions are uncovered on both sides, so the depletion region widens, the barrier grows and only the very small reverse current flows.
common_mistakes: Saying no current at all flows in reverse bias. A very small reverse current flows, carried by minority carriers.
Saying the width does not change in reverse bias.

recall.must_convey: That in reverse bias the depletion layer becomes wider.

steps.memory_tip: Reverse bias blocks current, so it thickens the barrier.

insider_note: Two words carry the marks — decreases and increases. Add one line of reason each so a single wrong word does not cost the whole mark.
